corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, the corpus maps broad exploration of large language models in social science, spanning education, health, policy, and everyday life. It reveals recurring concerns about reliability, safety, and bias, alongside opportunities for AI-enabled learning, research methods, and governance. The literature highlights diverse human-AI interactions, social dynamics, and cross-domain analytics that demand careful validation and ethical framing.

themes.name: LLM reliability, safety, and governance in practice
themes.description: A cross-section of 2026 papers scrutinize LLM fallibility, safety, fairness, and the need for governance frameworks to mitigate misinformation, bias, and misleading behavior.

themes.name: AI-enhanced learning and education design
themes.description: Studies explore AI tutors, scaffolding, classroom integration, and AI literacy across school, higher education, and lifelong learning, assessing trust, engagement, pedagogy, and outcomes.

themes.name: Socio-technical dynamics of AI adoption and interaction
themes.description: A broad set of studies analyze how users trust, anthropomorphism, peer influence, social networks, and organizational contexts shape adoption, use, and collaboration with AI.

themes.name: AI as a cross-disciplinary research and policy instrument
themes.description: Papers show LLMs used to support research methods, policy analysis, climate and health governance, and cultural heritage, alongside methodological debates about validation and ethics.
